name: sockleak
description: apple/fgx#132: a loopback descriptor must never keep a W5100 hardware socket.  An AF_INET descriptor claims one only when a verb first drives the chip (_Xport_Claim); one bound or connected to 127/8 is stamped SOCK_HW_LOOP and gives back any it holds (_Loop_ReleaseHw), which matters for the wildcard listener whose hardware listen failed after claiming.  _W5_SockAlloc hands out all four (1..3 first, then 0, which /dev/bpf0 claims through the same bitmap for MACRAW), and teardown skips the free for anything >= W5_NSOCK, so a sentinel stamped over a held slot strands it for the boot.  THREE RUNS, NOT TWO: each loopprobe makes two socket() calls, so a loopback path that held slots has used all four by the end of the second run, and the third fails at socket().  It proves the slots are genuinely recycled rather than merely sufficient for one repeat.
